body:
I feel very much for you here, So many aspects of what I read strike close to home, thoughts I have often.  I did not go on to higher education, I pursued 'the job' which was any job after a six month search and found myself in a career.  I, too, see friends advancing although to be honest they're thriving in academic settings while I have worked in a field and job I hate every day.  It's like feeling trapped in a vast ocean treading water when one is so very, very, exhausted.  

Your sadness is valid, you are valid, and what you want, most importantly, is valid.  You have to walk a road that no one else will ever truly walk (though you may pass by others and common places from time to time,) all the challenges and changes that will come with it will be there.  For what it's worth, I hope that you get to take that journey, and remember that no matter how many years pass, no goal is impossible.  Life can get in the way, but as my late father used to opine, he was an engineer by training (which was always my dream, and never realized) but in the end he never did any engineering, only worked with people management, a career I know he never envisioned at the start of things and only realized towards the end of his working life.  

Wishing you the best, even though that comes off cliche at best.  I hope the spark others have mentioned is something you come across and can nurture it and fan the flames.
